title: Scheme relative Proj represents Veronese invertible-quotient data
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $Z$ be an $S$-scheme, in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal B=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal B_n$ be a commutative unital graded $\mathcal O_Z$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures], with every degree quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]; no equality $\mathcal B_0=\mathcal O_Z$ or finite generation assumption is required. Pullbacks are tensor pullbacks [def-pc-module-pullback]. For $d\geq1$ write $\mathcal B^{(d)}_n=\mathcal B_{dn}$ with the inherited multiplication. For a quasi-compact $S$-scheme $T$, let $Q_{Z,\mathcal B}(T)$ be the set of equivalence classes of data $(d,f,\mathcal L,\psi)$, where $d\geq1$, $f:T\to Z$ is an $S$-morphism, $\mathcal L$ is an invertible $\mathcal O_T$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and $\psi:f^*\mathcal B^{(d)}\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$ is a graded unital algebra map whose degree-one component $f^*\mathcal B_d\to\mathcal L$ is surjective as a map of sheaves. Two data $(d,f,\mathcal L,\psi)$ and $(d',f',\mathcal L',\psi')$ are equivalent if $f=f'$ and there are positive integers $a,a'$ with $m=ad=a'd'$ and an isomorphism $\beta:\mathcal L^{\otimes a}\simeq(\mathcal L')^{\otimes a'}$ such that, for every $n\geq0$, $\beta^{\otimes n}\circ\psi_{an}=\psi'_{a'n}$ on $f^*\mathcal B_{mn}$, using the canonical tensor-power identifications. For arbitrary $T$ set $Q_{Z,\mathcal B}(T)=\varprojlim_{V\subseteq T\ \mathrm{quasi\text{-}compact\ open}}Q_{Z,\mathcal B}(V)$. The transition maps are restriction; pullback along $u:T'\to T$ is induced locally by $(d,f,\mathcal L,\psi)\mapsto(d,f\circ u,u^*\mathcal L,u^*\psi)$. These prescriptions give a set-valued contravariant functor on $S$-schemes. There is a canonical natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Mor}_S(T,\operatorname{Proj}_Z(\mathcal B))\simeq Q_{Z,\mathcal B}(T),$$
where the scheme on the left is the glued relative Proj [def-nagata-relative-proj]; composing a morphism on the left with its structural map to $Z$ corresponds on the right to remembering $f$. The bijection is the one induced by the canonical graded map to the twisting sheaves on relative Proj: over each affine open $V\subseteq Z$, on the chart $\pi^{-1}(V)\simeq\operatorname{Proj}(\Gamma(V,\mathcal B))$ of [def-nagata-relative-proj] with twisting sheaves $\mathcal O(d)$ [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf], locally where $\mathcal O(d)$ is invertible and the degree-$d$ quotient is surjective it uses $\mathcal L=\mathcal O(d)$ and the maps to $\mathcal O(dn)=\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$. For a graded $\mathcal O_Z$-algebra isomorphism $e:\mathcal B\simeq\mathcal C$, the ordinary induced isomorphism $\operatorname{Proj}_Z(\mathcal C)\simeq\operatorname{Proj}_Z(\mathcal B)$ [def-sfb-relative-proj-iso-of-graded-iso] corresponds to $[d,f,\mathcal L,\psi]\mapsto[d,f,\mathcal L,\psi\circ f^*e^{(d)}]$.

source.place: Tags 01NW (lemma-equivalent-relative), 01NY (lemma-relative-proj), 01NZ (lemma-glueing-gives-functor-proj), including the definition of equation-proj immediately before 01NY and the canonical twisting-sheaf normalization in the second proof of 01NZ.

proof.text: Put $Y=\operatorname{Proj}_Z(\mathcal B)$. Use the twisting modules $E_j$, canonical map $\eta$ and opens $Y_d$ supplied by [lem-sfb-relative-proj-twists-degree-opens]. Thus on $Y_d$ there is normalized quotient data $(d,\pi,E_d,\eta^{(d)})$ and these data become their tensor powers when $d$ is replaced by a multiple. The opens $Y_d$ cover $Y$ and are directed by divisibility. In particular this construction fixes the twisting-sheaf normalization required in the statement before any representing bijection is chosen.

Fix $d$ and data $(d,f,L,\psi)$ on any $T$. For an affine $V\subseteq Z$ put $W=f^{-1}V$ and $A=\Gamma(V,\mathcal B)$. Tensor-pullback adjunction followed degreewise by the affine tilde--sections adjunction identifies $\psi|_W$ with an $\mathcal O_Z(V)$-linear graded ring map $A^{(d)}\to\Gamma_*(W,L|_W)$. Naturality of the adjunction makes its unit and multiplication equations exactly those for $\psi$. Since $\mathcal B_d|_V$ is the tilde of $A_d$, its pullback is locally generated by $1\otimes a$, $a\in A_d$; hence these sections generate $L|_W$. Apply [lem-sfb-proj-fixed-degree-line-quotient] to obtain a unique morphism $g_V:W\to Y_d\cap\pi^{-1}V$ and a normalized isomorphism $g_V^*E_d\simeq L|_W$. The degree-zero equation, restricted to $\mathcal O_Z(V)\to A_0$, says $\pi g_V=f|_W$. For two affine base opens, refine their intersection by affine opens. The relative twisting identifications commute with restriction, so both local pairs pull the same universal data back to $\psi$; uniqueness in the fixed-degree lemma on each refinement makes the pairs equal there. Glue the maps by scheme-morphism gluing. The isomorphisms glue sectionwise as maps of sheaves, since they agree on overlaps. Conversely pulling back the universal data on $Y_d$ recovers this pair on every affine base open. Thus maps $T\to Y_d$ over $Z$ classify fixed-degree data up to strict isomorphism, without any quasi-compactness assumption on $T$.

source.place: 01NU (lemma-relative-proj-affine), 01NV (lemma-relative-proj-d), with affine refinements for all overlaps.

proof.text: Passing from $(d,f,L,\psi)$ to $(ad,f,L^{\otimes a},\psi_{a\bullet})$ gives valid data: locally lift a free generator $e$ of $L$ through the surjection $f^*\mathcal B_d\to L$; its $a$th power maps to $e^{\otimes a}$, proving degree-one surjectivity for the new data. The universal multiplication identifications on $Y_d$ show that this operation keeps the associated map $g:T\to Y$ unchanged. Now two data equivalent at some common multiple $m$ give strictly isomorphic degree-$m$ data, hence the same $g$ by step 2. Conversely if they give the same $g$, take $m=\operatorname{lcm}(d,d')$. The image lies in $Y_d\cap Y_{d'}\subseteq Y_m$, and the two powered line modules identify with $g^*E_m$. Composing these identifications gives $\beta:L^{\otimes(m/d)}\simeq(L')^{\otimes(m/d')}$ respecting every homogeneous component, including degree zero. Therefore the proposed equivalence is exactly equality of associated morphisms (and includes equality of $f=\pi g$). It is an equivalence relation. In particular all fixed-degree transition maps on strict classes are injective.

source.place: 01NW (lemma-equivalent-relative), using the fixed-degree classification proved in step 2; the local generator argument supplies surjectivity.

proof.text: Suppose $T$ is quasi-compact. Given $g:T\to Y$, the inverse images of the $Y_d$ form an open cover of $T$. Choose a finite subcover indexed by $d_1,\ldots,d_r$ and a positive common multiple $m$; then $g(T)\subseteq Y_m$. Pullback of the universal data on $Y_m$ gives a quadruple. Step 2 recovers $g$, and step 3 identifies exactly all quadruples producing it, independently of $m$. For $T=\varnothing$ take $m=1$. Restricting to maps over $S$ is equivalent to requiring that the remembered map $f=\pi g$ be over $S$, since $Y\to S$ factors through $Z$. This proves the required bijection for quasi-compact $S$-schemes and the structural-map assertion.

For arbitrary $T$, a compatible family in the stated inverse limit gives morphisms $g_V:V\to Y$ for every quasi-compact open $V\subseteq T$ by step 4. Affine opens form a basis, are quasi-compact, and cover every overlap $V\cap V'$; compatibility on these affine subopens makes $g_V$ and $g_{V'}$ agree on the whole overlap. Scheme-morphism gluing gives a unique $g:T\to Y$. Conversely restrictions of $g$ give that family. If $T$ itself is quasi-compact its component determines the family, so this also agrees with step 4. No intersection is assumed quasi-compact.

source.place: equation-proj before 01NY (lemma-relative-proj), with the gluing argument made explicit.

proof.text: For a morphism $u:T'\to T$ and a quasi-compact open $W\subseteq T'$, the image $u(W)$ is quasi-compact: pull an open cover back to $W$ and take a finite subcover. It is contained in a finite union $V$ of affine opens of $T$, hence in a quasi-compact open $V$ (an open cover of a finite union has a finite subcover on each member). Pull a representative of the $V$-component back along $W\to V$. Locally a surjection to a free rank-one module has a right inverse (lift its generator); tensor pullback preserves that right inverse, so the pulled-back datum is valid. Equivalence is preserved by pulling back $\beta$ and its component equations. The fixed-degree classification identifies this datum with $g_V\circ u|_W$. Thus its class is independent of the choice of $V$ or representative, and these classes are compatible in $W$. The identities and composition laws follow from those for composing scheme maps and the inverse-limit bijection in step 5. This constructs the prescribed functor and proves naturality on all $S$-schemes, including morphisms between non-quasi-compact tests.

Finally let $e:\mathcal B\simeq\mathcal C$ be a graded algebra isomorphism. On an affine base and a degree-$d$ element $a$ of $\mathcal B$, the ordinary induced Proj isomorphism sends the chart fraction $b/a^k$ to $e(b)/e(a)^k$. For a quotient $\psi$ of $\mathcal C^{(d)}$, step 2 therefore sends the composite morphism to the quotient with degree-$k$ value $\psi_k(e(b))$: its fraction formula is $\psi_k(e(b))/\psi_1(e(a))^{\otimes k}$. Uniqueness of the normalized fixed-degree pair identifies its line module with $L$. These identifications agree on affine base overlaps, so the operation is exactly $[d,f,L,\psi]\mapsto[d,f,L,\psi\circ f^*e^{(d)}]$. Step 5 extends the equality to arbitrary tests componentwise. This also verifies that the already normalized bijection is the canonical one specified in the item.
